text:
anna_support: Hey team — CorpX reports repeated mid-stream disconnects when users switch from cellular->WiFi. They see partial output (last token missing) and are being billed for the partial responses. Happening on iOS/Android. Example client timestamp: 2026-03-15T14:02:11Z. Server logs attached below. Any quick triage steps?

ben_mobile: thanks. any correlation IDs? client SDK version? first guess is connection close from client during network handoff.

anna_support: Correlation: trace=tx-8f3c2a, model=gpt-large, route=/v1/stream. SDK: mobile-sdk-js v1.3.5. Customer sent server log snippet:

anna_support: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11.102Z] trace=tx-8f3c2a stream_id=stream-77 write error: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.1.2.3:51234: write: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T14:02:11.103Z] trace=tx-8f3c2a stream_id=stream-77 client_closed=true status=499
```

zoe_engineer: 499 indicates client closed before server finished sending. Could be network flip, or the client aborting due to its own timeout. Mobile SDK has a 30s inactivity timeout-ish? @ben_mobile can confirm.

ben_mobile: mobile-sdk-js v1.3.5 default client-side idle timeout is 20s for backgrounded network changes (we back off). But that shouldn't auto-abort on handoff. We do cancel on certain OS signals. Do we see any TCP RSTs in tcpdump?

anna_support: customer provided tcpdump capture around the event. There's an immediate FIN/RST after the switch. They said it happens when they walk into a building and phone moves from 5G -> Enterprise WiFi.

sam_sre: adding my checklist: 1) confirm server idle timeout and keepalive settings; 2) check proxy (ingress LB) logs for client IP flip; 3) look for correlation ID traces across LB and app. Can you paste LB log lines for tx-8f3c2a?

anna_support: LB shows two consecutive client IPs for same trace: 203.11.45.9 -> 10.1.2.3 within 150ms, then connection closed. LB log: `203.11.45.9 - - [15/Mar/2026:14:02:11 +0000] "GET /v1/stream ...` then immediately a second incoming connection from 10.1.2.3 with same user-agent. Looks like OS did fast-switch and created new socket.

zoe_engineer: that pattern (new socket, old socket closed) is consistent with OS-level network handoff where in-flight TCP gets torn down. For SSE/HTTP streaming that results in truncation unless the client re-requests with resume support. Our API currently does not have explicit resume for streaming.

ben_mobile: client-side mitigation: implement small reconnect/backfill logic — if client detects network change while stream incomplete, re-open stream and ask server for last-chunk-id or re-ask with same conversation id so server can re-generate missing tokens. But that requires idempotency at application layer.

sam_sre: immediate server-side mitigations we can try: - increase idle keepalive and TCP keepalive probes on LB to reduce premature closes during short flaps - allow short reconnection window where we buffer last N tokens for given trace id (experimental) - emit explicit heartbeat frames every 10s so client keeps socket alive during jitter.

zoe_engineer: note: sending heartbeat frames (e.g., `\n` or zero-length chunk) helps some mobile stacks, but a handoff that replaces socket will still drop. Buffering at server would need storage per-stream and policies to avoid resource blowup.

anna_support: customer is asking for root cause and immediate workaround. They've requested whether we can avoid billing for truncated streams. Any policy options?

sam_sre: billing policy aside, we can help them reduce incidence. For billing, escalate to finance/legal for one-off credit. I'll create INC ticket and a billing request.

deploy-bot: Created INC-2741 (client-mid-stream-handoff-corruption) assigned to eng-runtime.

ben_mobile: for a quick repro internally: on iOS device with mobile data enabled, start streaming chat via mobile-sdk-js, then in settings toggle WiFi on or join a different SSID. Observed behavior: client receives partial payload, then socket closed with RST. Repro is 8/10 on our test devices.

zoe_engineer: thanks. Action items: 1) eng-runtime to evaluate adding periodic SSE heartbeats + consider a short in-memory buffer keyed by trace id for 5s to support immediate reconnect backfill. 2) mobile SDK: quick patch to avoid aggressive local abort on network change, instead retry once with resume hint. 3) support to offer customer credit + recommended app-side change.

sam_sre: I'm going to collect end-to-end traces for tx-8f3c2a and add to INC-2741. Need full proxy+app logs, and optionally pcap. @anna_support can you upload the pcap to the ticket?

anna_support: uploaded pcap to INC-2741 and added customer's reproduction steps + device models. I'll also propose a temporary client-side change we can advise them to deploy (heartbeat + auto-retry).

ben_mobile: I'll prepare a small sample patch for mobile-sdk-js (v1.3.6) that: 
- sends a 15s heartbeat over SSE
- suppresses automatic abort on OS network-change signal once, and retries the stream with same conversation id
I'll link PR to INC-2741 shortly.

zoe_engineer: I'll prototype a short-lived buffer for last 2-3 token-chunks on the runtime side to see memory impact. If feasible we can roll as opt-in flag for high-risk customers.

sam_sre: thanks all. Closing loop: customer-facing reply drafted, telling customer we have a bug/enhancement workstream (INC-2741), recommended immediate mitigation (SDK heartbeat + retry), and offered a credit while we investigate. :thumbsup:

anna_support: sending reply now. Thanks everyone!
